name: WKSS Japan Address Helper
author: wkss

sections.description:
WKSS Japan Address Helper helps WooCommerce stores in Japan fill address fields from Japanese postal codes.

For normal customer address lookup, this plugin does not use AjaxZip3 or any external lookup API. Address lookup is performed against a local postal code database stored in WordPress.

The plugin connects to Japan Post only when an administrator manually runs the postal code database update from the settings screen.

Main Features

  • Supports WooCommerce checkout, cart, and account address forms.
  • Supports WooCommerce Blocks checkout and cart address field updates.
  • Helps fill prefecture, city, and town address fields from Japanese postal codes.
  • Uses a local postal code database for normal address lookup.
  • Does not send customer address lookup data to Japan Post or any external service during checkout or address entry.
  • Downloads official Japan Post postal code CSV data only when an administrator manually runs the postal database update.
  • Provides a tabbed settings screen for basic settings, address validation, postal code data, and implementation notes.
  • Adds address validation options to warn or block checkout when postal-code consistency or street/block details may be incorrect.
  • Checks postal code against prefecture and municipality using the local postal code database.
  • Performs server-side validation for both classic checkout and Checkout Block / Store API order placement.
  • Address validation can target billing address, shipping address, or both.
  • Warning and blocking messages can be edited from the settings screen.
  • Adds a settings link to the plugin list.
  • Shows the plugin version on the settings screen.

External Services

This plugin can download a postal code CSV file from Japan Post only when an administrator clicks the postal database update button in the settings screen.

What the service is used for

  • Downloading official Japanese postal code CSV data from Japan Post.

What data is sent and when

  • The server sends a request to Japan Post to download the ZIP file only when an administrator manually runs the postal database update.
  • No customer address, checkout data, or personal information is sent to Japan Post during address lookup.
  • The plugin does not contact Japan Post or any external service during customer checkout or address entry.

Service provider

  • Japan Post
  • Service information: https://www.post.japanpost.jp/service/search/zipcode/download/utf-zip.html
  • Terms: https://www.post.japanpost.jp/
  • Privacy policy: https://www.post.japanpost.jp/privacy.html

Customer address lookup uses the local postal code database stored in WordPress.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or later
  • PHP 7.4 or later
  • WooCommerce 7.0 or later for customer-facing address completion and checkout validation

Data retention and removal

Deleting the plugin normally retains its settings and local postal-code database so they can be reused after reinstalling. Temporary import and update-consent locks are removed.

To permanently remove WJAH settings and the local postal-code database, use the explicit complete-delete action in the Backup and Maintenance tab before deleting the plugin files.

Settings backup

The Backup and Maintenance tab can export and restore WJAH settings in JSON format or reset settings to their defaults. The large local postal-code database is not included in the settings backup and can be downloaded again from Japan Post.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from the WordPress plugin screen, or upload the plugin ZIP file.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. To use customer-facing address features, make sure WooCommerce is active.
  4. Open the WKSS Japan Address Helper settings screen under WooCommerce, or under Settings when WooCommerce is inactive.
  5. Update the postal code database if needed.
  6. Configure address validation options if you want to warn or block checkout when address details may be incomplete.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin send customer address data to an external service?

No. Customer address lookup uses the local postal code database stored in WordPress.

Does this plugin use AjaxZip3?

No. This plugin does not use AjaxZip3 for normal customer address lookup.

When does this plugin access Japan Post?

Only when an administrator manually runs the postal code database update from the settings screen.

Does this plugin support WooCommerce Blocks?

Yes. The plugin supports WooCommerce Blocks checkout and cart address field updates.

Is WooCommerce required?

WooCommerce is required for customer-facing address completion and checkout validation. Without WooCommerce, administrators can still activate the plugin, open its settings screen under Settings, and prepare or inspect the local postal-code database.

Can address validation stop checkout?

Yes. The address validation feature can be set to off, warning mode, or blocking mode. It can target billing address, shipping address, or both. In blocking mode, postcode/prefecture and postcode/city mismatches are rejected server-side before order placement.

Can a modified version use the WKSS name and branding?

The source code is distributed under GPL v2 or later. A third-party modified or redistributed version must not use WKSS, WAKAISS WORKS, 若井製作所, their product names, slugs, logos, official icons, developer or seller identity, domains, or wording that suggests an official, recommended, certified, or supported WKSS release. A minimal factual compatibility reference is permitted only when it does not imply an official relationship.

1.1.34

  • Limits the administration screen to postal-code data and maintenance tools when the supported address platform is inactive.
  • Removes platform-dependent settings, status cards, specifications, and integration descriptions from that inactive-state DOM while preserving all saved settings.
  • Keeps the v1.1.33 Checkout Blocks synchronization fix and all customer-facing address behavior unchanged.

1.1.33

  • Reconciles Checkout Blocks address state after WooCommerce’s delayed postcode update so a newly resolved prefecture and municipality are not replaced by the previous address snapshot.
  • Keeps the fix limited to Blocks address synchronization and preserves detailed address input, foreign-country protection, Classic Checkout behavior, settings, database, and administration behavior.

1.1.32

  • Keeps the Checkout Blocks prefecture and municipality synchronized when a postal code changes, while preserving detailed address input and foreign-country selections.

1.1.31

  • Added the MS-039 shared WKSS administration hub contract and canonical asset set without changing address or postal-data behavior.
  • Keeps a standard WordPress menu fallback when the shared hub contract or assets are incompatible.

1.1.30

  • Adds a clear waiting notice and live processing status for postal-code database updates and imports, including guidance not to close or reload the page until completion.

1.1.29

  • Keep Classic Checkout address updates out of the Blocks customer-data store so a stored JP country cannot overwrite a newly selected foreign country.

1.1.28

  • Cancel pending postal lookups when the checkout country changes, preventing a Classic Checkout re-render from applying a stale Japanese address to a foreign country selection.

1.1.27

  • Imports postal data into an isolated staging table and keeps the previous live database when parsing, insertion, or table replacement fails.
  • Expands postal town text storage so current official Japan Post rows are not rejected when kana content exceeds the previous field limit.
  • Prevents stale postcode results from being applied while a newer postcode lookup is pending.
  • Restricts Japanese postcode completion to Japanese or not-yet-selected country fields and no longer overwrites a selected foreign country.
  • Aligns frontend warnings with the configured validation target and adds address-line warning rules used by server-side validation.
  • Adds settings export, restore, and reset controls.
  • Adds an explicit complete-data deletion action while normal WordPress uninstall continues to retain settings and postal data.
  • Adds file-integrity status and one-time update consent protection.

1.1.23

  • Added the WKSS standard Compact Header with shared saved state, restore controls, server time, and synchronized description display.
  • Allowed activation and administration without WooCommerce; WooCommerce-specific customer address features remain unavailable until WooCommerce is active.
  • Documented the WKSS branding boundary for modified and redistributed versions.
  • Preserved the existing address lookup, validation, and postal database behavior.

1.1.22

  • Fixed postcode autofill for municipality fields in Cart and Checkout Blocks by synchronizing the official WooCommerce cart data store before DOM events.
  • Uses the native input/select value setter so React-controlled address fields recognize WJAH changes without affecting Classic Checkout.
  • Preserves user-entered street/building details and keeps the Address Core, Classic/Blocks server validation, settings, and database schema unchanged.

1.1.21

  • Escaped the Checkout Blocks validation exception message before passing it to the exception object.
  • Documented narrowly scoped direct-database-query exceptions for the plugin-owned postal-code table so Plugin Check can distinguish the intentional local dataset operations.
  • Kept the administration UI, settings, database schema, address lookup, Classic/Blocks validation behavior, and user-entered address protection unchanged.

1.1.20

  • Finalized the WJAH administration UI against the WKSS/WEM shared layout and information hierarchy.
  • Uses the official WJAH icon, semantic status cards, accessible tabs, responsive spacing, and a visually separated high-impact postal-data deletion area.
  • Keeps the existing tabs and adds an informational WKSS integration tab without adding plugin dependencies.
  • Does not add backup, restore, reset, postal-data import progress, or other processing behavior.
  • Kept all settings, option keys, database structures, hooks, imports, validation, and address logic unchanged from the v1.1.14 functional baseline.

1.1.18

  • Replaced the WEM-specific green administration accent with WJAH’s own restrained Japanese postbox-red palette.
  • Preserved the shared WEM layout structure, the official WJAH icon, and all existing settings and feature logic.

1.1.17

  • Aligned the administration shell with the current WEM layout: wider identity column, stable 2-by-2 status cards, green suite header treatment, menu guidance placement, tabs, and spacing.
  • Removed the redundant visible status strip below the tabs because the same state remains available in the header cards.
  • Kept the official WJAH icon and all existing settings, hooks, database structures, validation, import, and address logic unchanged.

1.1.16

  • Replaced the temporary letter badge with the official WKSS WJAH icon from the approved WKSS icon package.
  • Kept all settings, hooks, database structures, validation, import, and address logic unchanged.

  • Unified the administration screen with the current WKSS/WEM visual and information structure.
  • Added the WKSS suite icon, semantic status labels, compact expert summaries, and accessible current-tab state.
  • Visually separated postal-data deletion as a high-impact operation without changing its processing.
  • Added an informational WKSS integration tab; no plugin dependency or integration logic was added.
  • Added a visible saving state to existing settings forms.
  • Kept all existing settings, option keys, database structures, hooks, validation, imports, and address logic unchanged.

  • Tracks WJAH-managed town values by billing/shipping scope in page memory so WooCommerce Blocks re-renders do not lose safe replacement state.
  • Replaces a previous auto-filled town only when the current value still exactly matches WJAH’s managed value; shopper-entered house numbers and other edits remain untouched.
  • Recovers safe town ownership when the current address line contains only the exact town from the previously resolved postcode.
  • Ignores stale postcode lookup responses when a shopper changes postcodes before an earlier request finishes.

  • Fixed postcode changes so a town previously auto-filled by WJAH is safely replaced with the new postcode’s town.
  • Keeps detailed user-entered street and house-number text unchanged in empty-only mode.
  • Applies the same safe town-replacement rule to WooCommerce Checkout Blocks customer data.

  • Fixed postal-code autofill so prefecture and municipality are corrected even when stale values already exist.
  • Added WooCommerce Japanese prefecture-code synchronization (JP01-JP47) for Checkout Blocks.
  • Preserved the configured overwrite policy for town/street/house-number fields so existing detailed addresses are not erased in empty-only mode.
  • Reapplies deterministic prefecture/city data when the same cached postcode is processed again.

  • Split address analysis into an adapter-neutral core and a WooCommerce adapter.
  • Added local postal-code database consistency checks for prefecture and municipality.
  • Added server-side Checkout Block / Store API validation so blocking mode does not depend on JavaScript address completion.
  • Added scoped frontend mismatch warnings for WooCommerce address fields.
  • Preserved existing settings and existing incomplete-address checks.
